questions.question: Compare internal and external recruitment, giving two advantages of each.

points.text: Internal recruitment advantages: quicker (already knows the business), cheaper (no advertising or onboarding), motivating (shows promotion is possible), known performance. External recruitment advantages: wider talent pool (more candidates), fresh perspectives and ideas, avoids internal resentment/politics, brings new skills the business lacks.

questions.question: Explain why a job description and person specification are both needed in the recruitment process.

points.text: The job description defines WHAT the role involves (duties, responsibilities, reporting lines, salary) so candidates know what they are applying for. The person specification defines WHO is needed (qualifications, skills, experience, qualities) so the business can fairly assess candidates against consistent criteria. markScheme.exemplarAnswer: A grade 9 response will: analyse the agency route (access to pre-screened candidates, saves management time, professional expertise, but costs 15-25% of salary); direct advertising (cheaper, shows independence, but limited reach, time-consuming screening, owner may lack interview skills); consider business context (small business needs the right person urgently, a bad hire is very costly for a small team, but the agency fee could be £5,000-£10,000); conclude: for a critical management role, the agency investment is justified because the cost of a poor hire (lost productivity, re-recruitment, team disruption) far exceeds the agency fee.
